description: A director of career and technical education must authorize the reopening of a metal-fabrication lab and finalize its enrollment, respiratory protection, fire-watch procedure, and instructional staffing plan, with input from the lab instructor, district safety officer, school nurse, and industry-partnership coordinator.

agents.name: Dr. Morgan
agents.role: Director of Career and Technical Education

shared_context.S1: The metal-fabrication lab has been closed while the school prepares a revised operating plan.
shared_context.S2: The draft plan proposes reopening the lab for up to 20 students with standard protective equipment, ordinary end-of-class cleanup, and Ms. Ortiz as the instructor.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Morgan has authority to approve the reopening and set binding operating requirements.
shared_context.S4: The school's normal pre-authorization routine is to ask the instructor, safety officer, nurse, and industry-partnership coordinator for final information before a specialized lab is reopened.

PF1.text: Ms. Ortiz's completed airflow test found that the lab's current ventilation system supports no more than 12 students working in the booths at one time; she submitted the test to maintenance this week, but the revised operating-plan folder has not been updated.

PF2.text: Mr. Shah's fire-code review requires a hot-work permit for every lab session and a continuous 30-minute fire watch after welding ends; he finalized the review this week, but the approval packet still contains the ordinary cleanup procedure.

PF3.text: Two students registered for the lab have health plans requiring a powered air-purifying respirator during welding, and the school has two compatible units available; Nurse Williams confirmed the plans and equipment this week, but has not entered the requirement in the lab plan.

PF4.text: The insurer's credential file shows that Ms. Ortiz's welding-instructor credential expired last month; it authorizes reopening only with Mr. Bell, whose current credential is verified, as lead instructor on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Ms. Becker received the insurer's confirmation this week, but it has not been forwarded to Dr. Morgan.

acceptance_conditions: Enrollment must be capped at exactly 12 students.
Powered air-purifying respirators must be required for welding.
A hot-work permit must be required for every lab session.
A continuous 30-minute post-welding fire watch must be required.
Mr. Bell must be the lead instructor.
Instruction must occur on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
The operating plan must contain a formal safety-compliance commitment.

decisive_facts.why: The airflow test changes the enrollment cap from the draft 20 students to exactly 12 students.
The fire-code review changes the procedure from ordinary cleanup to a permit for every session and an exact 30-minute fire watch, requiring a safety-compliance record.
The two students' health plans change respiratory protection from standard equipment to powered air-purifying respirators.
The insurer's credential condition changes the lead instructor from Ms. Ortiz to Mr. Bell and changes the operating days to Tuesday/Thursday.
